is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluates mosquito trapping schemes capturing Anopheles funestus s.l. and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (page 6, Table 1; page 9).

reports_target_markers.evidence: PCR was performed only for species identification within the An. gambiae complex and An. funestus group (page 6, 'Mosquito processing in the laboratory'; page 9). No insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No insecticide-resistance marker genotype or allele data are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Luangwa and Nyimba districts, Zambia between 2011 and 2013 (pages 3-5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study evaluating community-based mosquito trapping methods and surveillance.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were conducted in 14 population clusters around specific health facilities in Luangwa and Nyimba districts, Zambia (pages 3-4, Figure 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Sampling took place between January 2011 and April 2013 (page 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine field study evaluation in Zambia; no overlap with larger consortia genomic databases.

supplement.evidence: No missing supplementary material indicated as containing target resistance marker data.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness and epidemiological relevance of community-based mosquito trapping using CDC light traps and Ifakara tent traps in Luangwa and Nyimba districts, Zambia. While PCR was used for species identification and ELISA for sporozoite detection, no insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped.
exclusion_reasons: Does not genotype any of the target insecticide-resistance markers (PCR was strictly for species identification within species complexes/groups).
No extractable resistance marker genotype data reported.
